newsitem.title: UK: IPE oil futures firm on Iraqi export news.
newsitem.headline: IPE oil futures firm on Iraqi export news.

text.p: IPE Brent crude futures inched higher in quiet early trade on Monday, as news at the weekend of a delay to Iraqi crude exports and tighter North Sea markets continued to support prices, brokers said.
August Brent contract opened 17 cents up at $18.35 a barrel but bounced off key resistance at $18.45, last week's high, to settle back around $18.30 in early business.

Brokers said with no fresh news to move prices, a statement from Iraq's United Nations negotiator that exports might resume in August pending U.N. approval of a plan for distribution of food and medical supplies in Iraq was holding up the market.
"After Friday's stable close, people are still focusing on the Iraqi news," said Tony Machachek, broker at Credit Lyonnais Rouse.

"But I wouldn't have thought that would justify the rise in prices this morning. It's likely with the lack of interest in selling, someone's been doing some aggressive bidding to try and put some higher numbers on the board."
Dealers said they expected volume to remain fairly subdued for the rest of the week, especially in the U.S. where NYMEX will be closed on Friday and close early on Thursday.
July gas oil stood $1.50 a tonne firmer at $165.25 after opening above initial treble-top resistance at $164.50 and filling a small gap to $164.75 a tonne.
"More significantly the gap between $170.75 and $171.50 will be the first objective with a ceiling around $175," said Nicholas Wilson at MeesPierson Isle of Man.
